sources.title: Detectability and impact of repetitive surveys on threatened West African crocodylians
sources.locator: Abstract; occupancy model; survey-effort estimates and effects of fishing-net encounters.
sources.scope: Repeated surveys at 38 sites in Côte d'Ivoire from 2014 to 2019, studying detection of M. cataphractus and C. suchus; conclusions are conditional on the study area and survey design.
sources.attribution: Ahizi MN, Kouman CY, Ouattara A, Kouamé NP, Dede A, Fairet E, Shirley MH (2021). Detectability and impact of repetitive surveys on threatened West African crocodylians. Ecology and Evolution 11(21):15062–15076. DOI 10.1002/ece3.8188. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: The occupancy-based model estimated mean M. cataphractus detection probability at 0.75; two surveys were needed to infer absence with 90% confidence under the modeled conditions, and fishing-net encounter rate negatively affected detection.
claims.scope: Model estimates for the sampled Côte d'Ivoire sites and covariates, not an abundance estimate or causal range-wide result.

gaps: The study does not estimate population size across the species range.
Detection and fishing associations should not be interpreted as range-wide causal effects.
